purpose: Audio orchestration defaults shared by pycore (pyctl/audio_orchestration), the pycore-manager UI and the wordnew client composer (shared/orchestration). docs_fix/DESIGN_AUDIO_ORCHESTRATION.md, docs_fix/DESIGN_WORDNEW_CLIENT.md.

transfer.purpose: Clip transfer between pycore / Laravel and the clients. Many small clips move as framed bundles (one request, no per-file round trip): pycore ui/audio_orch/resource/bundle and Laravel /api/app_qy_v1/ai_tools/tts/audio/bundle answer the same frame. pycore also serves one clip raw (resource/file, GET); Laravel answers URL batches (sentence/audio/head, word/audio/head). Clients keep at most the per-backend parallel limit of transfers in flight (device setting, default parallel_defaults, 1..parallel_max); the native app writes bundle frames straight to disk.
transfer.pycore_bundle_frame: per request item, in order: 4-byte big-endian header length, UTF-8 JSON header {index, key, hit, bytes, sent, meaning, version?}, then `bytes` payload bytes when sent is true (a hit past the byte budget is sent:false and is asked again)

content_update.purpose: Server-declared content update of a held clip (WORDNEW_GUIDE R14, the only automatic exception). Laravel reports a clip's `version` (the mtime in seconds of the file it serves, 0 or null when it holds none) in the bundle frame header and, when the audio/lookup request sets with_version, in every lookup result (with the url of that very file: a sentence quality variant is named, not the default file). The app records the version of each clip it stores and replaces only the clips whose reported version differs from the recorded one; a clip stored without a version records the first reported version without any download.

book_plan.purpose: Server-owned audio plan of one book. The client posts the plan once (book, languages, reading position); Laravel derives the required clips from its own book data, raises their gap rows by reading position and keeps counters; the client follows by cursor and downloads only newly ready clips. Every node generates through work leases.

assignments_request.from: int: sentence seq the windows start at (the reader position)
assignments_request.windows: [{sid, lane, language, count}] in play order; sid is a work node's short id or the device direct sid (direct_window_sid); count = pending clips of that lane and language the node takes, laid out one after another from `from`, per lane and language independently
assignments_request.device_id: string, at most 16 chars: the posting app device; required for direct windows
assignments_request.direct_node_sid: optional work node sid of the app's direct pycore when it is also a Laravel work node (its node ranges then never overlap the device's direct ranges)

book_plan.direct_window_sid: direct_sid + ':' + device_id[0:6]. Laravel treats every window sid starting with direct_sid as a direct window (no lease: every node's claim skips its rows). An app posts direct windows only for the (lane, language) pairs its direct pycore can generate (lane_capability).
book_plan.assignments_layout_rule: Node windows are per plan (last writer wins; the relayout signature covers node windows only, so direct windows never force a node relayout). Direct windows are kept per (plan, device_id) with their own assignment_ttl_seconds heartbeat, so several devices each hold their direct range and do not thrash each other; a post with windows [] drops that device's direct ranges.
book_plan.assignments_rule: App-led scheduling. While the app is open it computes the windows from the roster it knows (Laravel nodes with lanes, class and throughput, plus its direct pycore) and POSTs them; each POST is the plan heartbeat. Laravel resolves every window to a position range of the plan's pending clips and, for assignment_ttl_seconds after the last POST, leases a window's rows only to its node (the node claims them first, every other node's claim skips them; direct_sid windows are skipped by all nodes: the direct pycore generates them). When the heartbeat expires (the app closed) the ranges are dropped and the claims fall back to Laravel's own fair share. Ranges are re-laid out on a changed window set, a reader move of reprioritize_min_move or every assignment_relayout_seconds.
book_plan.assignments_response: {fresh, expires_in, windows: [{sid, lane, assigned, generating, done}]}: per node and lane, summed over languages; assigned and done are cumulative over the plan (relayouts carry finished clips), generating is the live leases inside the node's current ranges. The app sizes a window as the node's items per hour x assignment_horizon_minutes (at least assignment_min_clips)

plan_request.languages: sentence languages the plan voices (iso codes)
plan_request.include_words: bool: also the distinct words of the primary-language sentences
plan_request.include_phrases: bool: also the distinct phrases (phrase_pipeline) of the primary-language sentences; phrase rows are leased on lane phrase_audio
plan_request.position: int: sentence seq the reader is at (priority is raised from there forward)
plan_request.plan_hash: client plan hash (idempotence marker, at most 64 chars)

status_response.generating: int clips under a live lease
status_response.failed: int clips whose retry budget ran out
status_response.empty_languages: [language] requested sentence languages that hold no clip yet (their sentences are not in the library; the server adds them by itself once they are)
status_response.ready_cursor: int, the highest ready sequence handed out (0 = none)
status_response.nodes: [{sid, label, platform, compute_class, count}] clips of the plan each node generates now
status_response.assignments: assignments_response of the plan (fresh false when no app heartbeat is live)
status_response.fast_pass: bool: the plan runs its sentence fast pass
status_response.upgrade: {total, done}: fast-pass sentences and those already upgraded by the quality pass

ready_response.ids: [resource id] ready clips after the cursor (sha256 resource ids, ready sequence order)
ready_response.cursor: int, pass it as the next request's cursor

fast_pass.rule: DISABLED (enabled=false): sentences of a floor language are accepted only from its quality-floor engine (queue_center_contract work_leases.sentence_quality.accepted_engines_by_language); other languages accept any engine. When enabled, a plan whose missing sentences exceed missing_threshold runs the fast pass: any node whose sentence lane declares the fast engine (cpu or gpu, Colab-CPU included) may lease that plan's sentence rows with engine_hint = engine and delivers the base clip; once delivered, a gpu node whose lane declares quality_engine may lease the row again as an upgrade (variant_key = quality_variant, engine_hint = quality_engine) and delivers the quality variant next to the base clip. Clients play the clip that is ready: the quality variant when the server holds it, else the base.

client_monitor.purpose: Latest-state telemetry of every open wordnew client for the laravel-manager orchestration monitor. Never outboxed, never an availability source (R7).

auth.monitor: operator session or client key (like work/nodes)

report_request.instance_id: string, at most 64 chars (one app run)
report_request.channels: {direct, relay, laravel, lan: bool, selected_pycore: {host, node_sid}, laravel_endpoint_id}
report_request.tasks: [{task_id, plan_id|null, state, counts: {<kind>: {lane, total, queued, loading, done, missing, generating: {pycore, relay, laravel}}}, stages: {<stageId>: state}}] at most max_tasks
report_request.assignments: [{plan_id, fresh, expires_in, direct_share: {<lane>: n}, windows: [{sid, lane, language, count, assigned, generating, done}]}]

client_monitor.report_response: {accepted: bool, stale: bool}: stale = a seq not newer than the stored one of the same (device_id, instance_id), dropped
client_monitor.rule: Laravel keeps one entry per (user, device_id, instance_id) in cache for ttl_seconds after its last report (latest wins, an older or equal seq is dropped as stale); a client never reports more often than min_interval_seconds (it reports every report_seconds and on a route, channel or task change). A changed state (seq and sent_at ignored) or an expired client emits the throttled realtime event orch_clients.changed (queue_center_contract realtime.orch_clients_changed). The monitor lists clients with user, last_seen_at and online (younger than ttl_seconds).

step_options.meaning: word steps only: after each word, read its short Chinese meaning (wordnew implements it; pycore: open item in docs_fix/DESIGN_AUDIO_ORCHESTRATION.md); phrases steps: after each phrase, read its Chinese meaning (a zh sentence clip of the meaning text)

phrase_pipeline.purpose: Every live sentence gets AI-extracted phrases (idempotent); every phrase gets audio. Binding: docs_fix/DESIGN_PHRASE_PIPELINE.md.
phrase_pipeline.identity: content_id = media_content_id(phrase text) (md5 of collapse_ws(lower(strip P/S))); resource_id = sha256('phrase:<language>:<content_id>')

model_selection.rule: request_options.models stays the preferred pinned list. The selector (AppQyV1PhraseModelSelector) keeps the pinned ids the live free catalog still lists, tops the list up to max_models from that catalog (free, text output, context >= min_context_length, every required_parameters entry supported, id not matching exclude_id_patterns, prefer_id_patterns first) and skips models in cooldown. A model that answers with reasoning text only, an unparseable or truncated answer, or an unavailable-model error collects strikes (strike_weights); strike_limit strikes put it in cooldown_seconds cooldown. With every candidate cooled the extractor backs off all_cooled_backoff_seconds.

failure_policy.rule: A provider or model fault is not the sentences' fault: uncharged_codes, uncharged_marks (an invalid key) and model_error_marks release the claimed sentences without a phrase attempt and back the extractor off backoff_seconds (model_error_marks also strike the model). model_strike_codes charge the attempt (the batch itself may be too heavy) and strike the model. Rate limit, quota and unconfigured provider keep going through pycore_fallback_codes.

extraction.rule: OpenRouter free tier (openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits): 20 requests/min, 50/day without credits, 1000/day with >= 10 credits; free models have >= 32k context, so a batch is at most batch_sentences sentences and batch_max_chars input chars (about 750 tokens) with max_output_tokens for the JSON answer, which keeps one request well inside every free model's window and under request_timeout_seconds while spending the daily budget on many sentences per request. model is pinned to free instruct models with JSON mode (request_options.models is the OpenRouter in-request fallback list, free ids only; re-check the free catalog GET /api/v1/models when they disappear): the random openrouter/free router picked reasoning models and the nemotron content-safety guard. request_options ask for JSON mode and reasoning off (effort none, excluded; with only low effort the models still spent the token budget thinking and returned empty content, finish_reason length; measured 2026-10-05 with 40-sentence batches: timeouts, reasoning-only and guard answers). Laravel claims a batch of sentences without phrases (phrase lease columns), calls the gateway itself (AI gateway rule); on a pycore_fallback_codes failure it hands the batch to pycore as one global_tasks row of pycore_task_type (at most pycore_tasks_max_pending open), and pycore answers with its own OpenRouter free key. A sentence whose answer lists no phrase is phrase_status none (done, never retried); a failure adds one attempt and after max_attempts the sentence is failed until sys:init or the resurface sweep returns it.

audio.rule: Phrase audio is a work-lease lane over the per-language phrase table (tts_* lease columns, like sentences). CPU engines are accepted (kokoro batch, like words); gpu nodes may serve it with spare capacity. A phrase already stored with audio is never regenerated; an existing phrase without audio stays in the gap.

phrase_pipeline.scheduling: While a wordnew orchestration page is open and connected to an online pycore, wordnew is the primary phrase-audio scheduler (generate:pycore with kind phrase, book-plan R12 windows on lane phrase_audio), Laravel secondary (want exclusion, fallback leases). Otherwise Laravel is the primary scheduler (work leases to every node). Phrase extraction (text) is always scheduled by Laravel (Octane timer), with pycore as the fallback executor.
